newsitem.title: USA: Somanetics Q4, year hurt by lower revenues.
newsitem.headline: Somanetics Q4, year hurt by lower revenues.

text.p: Somanetics Corp, a development stage company that markets the Cerebral Oximeter monitoring system, said its November 30 fourth quarter and year-end results were hurt by lower revenues and a two-fold increase in company personnel.

The added personnel came between May 31, 1996 and November 30, 1996 in connection with the start of U.S. selling and marketing activities following Food and Drug Administration clearance of its product.
It also cited research and development expenses relating to an agreement with NeuroPhysics Corp regarding four new products and in-house new product development programs.
In the fourth quarter, Somanetics posted a loss of $0.09 a share and for the full year, a loss of $0.18 a share. Total revenues for the year declined to $778,000 from $1.3 million.
The company said it plans to invest significant resources in fiscal 1997 to selling and marketing activities and research and development of new product programs.
